raw_response:
I farm 12 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, so this same 12 mu will go through wheat first and then maize. I have done this for many years, so I will not change too much unless there is a clear reason. With well irrigation, I do not dare save too much on water or fertilizer, because once yield falls, that loss is bigger than the extra few bags of input. On my land in Quzhou, wheat has to stand strong before winter and fill grain well in spring, so I will put a solid base fertilizer down, then chase nitrogen later. For maize after wheat, I will still use hybrid seed, because that gives steadier yield here and most people around me use it. I will keep fertilizer a bit on the safe side, not too low. If I am unsure, I would rather add a little more nitrogen than watch the crop stay pale. For wheat I will irrigate around 3 times if the season is normal, and for maize about 2 times with the well. Pesticide I will not spray blindly, but I will plan for about 2 sprays on each crop, because rust, aphids, armyworm, and leaf disease can all cost yield if I wait too long. Wheat I will mostly rotary till after maize residue, and maize after wheat I will also use rotary tillage for speed, because 12 mu is enough that I care about getting through the season on time, but not so big that I must strip every cost to the bone.
